title: Returning does not mean stopping
storyboard: The released cube crosses the zero line instead of stopping there. Returning to the position/velocity study from Fields, the student adapts it to one axis and reuses Kinetic Forces’ resistance term. They own the force sum, minus stiffness times displacement minus damping times velocity, and its update: velocity changes by force divided by mass times the step; displacement then uses the new velocity. The runner, rail and handle remain supplied. Before release, they predict the restoring direction and explain why zero spring force at the centre need not mean zero motion. Equal beginnings under two damping settings test the prediction. This computed return differs from Transformation’s prescribed sine. The learner keeps a small oscillator they can vary, without assuming the museum has transported a shared state or transferred a hand throw.
storyboard_short: Return to Fields’ proposed position/velocity study in one dimension; add restoration and Kinetic Forces’ damping. Own F = -kx - cv, then v += (F/m)dt and x += vdt. Supply runner, rail and handle; release starts from rest. Predict force direction and crossing, compare damping from equal beginnings, and carry the oscillator toward later waves. Distinguish computed motion from prescribed sine; no shared museum-state or hand-throw transfer is implied.
brings: vector/force addition and Transformation’s prescribed sine comparison
learns: displacement-dependent restoring force combined with velocity-dependent damping
equilibrium position and rest are different conditions
the order of velocity and position updates matters in a numerical model
carries: A scalar spring-damper update with declared beginning and coefficients, reusable in later oscillator studies; future coupled waves will additionally need separate old/new states across receivers.
supplied: fixed 1/120 s runner and finite observation cutoff
rail, constrained pickable handle and display
parameter controls and reset/release adapter; release sets velocity to zero
review_note: Summary proposal only. The installed restoring_forces variant computes scalar motion; its frozen pickable is input/display, not another body solver. k is N/m, c is kg/s, and F/m is acceleration, not F/dt. DAMP selects a ratio and computes c = 2*ratio*sqrt(k*m); changing mass or stiffness therefore changes c at a fixed nonzero ratio. Hold m and k fixed for the damping comparison. Parameter changes preserve state, whereas release starts from rest. The common learner update and its edit binding remain proposed, with manual reuse rather than automatic transport. Keep legacy cosine towers distinct; do not add a full numerical-methods lesson.
independent_check: At x = +1.25 m and v = 0, with k = 8 N/m and m = 2 kg, predict restoring force -10 N and initial acceleration -5 m/s². Under FREE damping, predict negative velocity at the first crossing of x = 0 even though spring force is zero there. Repeat from the same displacement, mass and stiffness under LIGHT damping; predict smaller later excursions. Use reset/release between trials, and distinguish a predicted centre crossing from an exactly sampled zero.
change_reason: The sequence deepens a usable state model rather than restarting with another animation, while preserving the room’s question of return, rest and motion.
